messages:
sara (oncall): paging — multiple customers reporting login loops and 401s in the last 10m. console access also intermittently 502ing for some users. tagging eng-sre and platform.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager duty notification sent to sara (oncall), alyssa (eng-sre). Incident created: INC-2026-0459.
mike (platform): I'm seeing elevated 5xx from our auth proxy to auth0-edge in us-west-2. Upstream responses include 503 and occasional malformed jwks responses. curl shows `Content-Type: application/json` but body is truncated.
alyssa (eng-sre): rolling through logs — verifier errors: "jwt: invalid signature" and a few "jwks parse error: unexpected EOF". Looks like intermittent truncated jwks fetches. Could be Auth0 CDN/edge or dns failovers.
sara (oncall): impact assessment: initial alert from 3 customer accounts (payments, billing-ui, internal-admin). CS already getting tickets. @cs-lead please triage priority customers and collect SLO-impact.
cs-lead: on it. Reached out to top 10 active customers in the last hour, 4 confirmed login failures, one has admin console down. Escalating to account execs.
mike (platform): mitigation idea: switch our jwks provider cache to "stale-while-revalidate" fallback to local cached JWKS to avoid signature rejections for 10m. We have cached keys from last successful fetch at /var/cache/auth0/jwks.json.
alyssa (eng-sre): agree. Quick safe change: enable env var AUTH0_JWKS_FALLBACK=1 in auth-verifier deployment and bump jwks cache TTL to 600s. That avoids rejecting tokens during fetch errors. I'll prepare rollout.
sara (oncall): do it. Post rollback plan in thread.
alyssa (eng-sre): applying: kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-verifier AUTH0_JWKS_FALLBACK=1 && kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/auth-verifier
deploy-bot: ^^^ k8s rollout initiated by alyssa at 2026-03-15T15:12:42Z. Pod restarts: 3/3 updated.
mike (platform): also rate-limiting our jwks fetches to avoid thundering herd against auth0: `jwks_fetch_interval = max(60, jittered_backoff)` and add exponential backoff on 5xx.
sara (oncall): added a temporary traffic routing rule: route auth traffic to secondary region (eu-west-1) for new sessions while fallback is enabled. That should reduce load on the failing edge.
alyssa (eng-sre): verifier logs show JWKS fallback kicking in, "using cached jwks (age 42s)". Token verifications returning to normal for most requests.
cs-lead: CS report: 3 customers fully recovered, 1 still seeing console 502s — probably admin console hosted in us-west-2. We're sending interim notice: "We are aware of login and console access issues caused by an upstream auth provider outage; mitigations in progress."
sara (oncall): update status page draft: "Degraded authentication: affected customers may see login failures and console errors. We have enabled fallback JWKS and rerouted sessions; full restoration depends on upstream provider. Next update in 30m"
mike (platform): reach out to Auth0 support with request id + example truncated payloads. I have pcap and curl captures. Sending to their SRE now.
alyssa (eng-sre): watch for signature mismatch regressions — if fallback causes any compatibility issues we can enable stricter validation per route, but prioritize availability for now.
incident-bot: on-call handoff scheduled in 45m. Next on-call: jordan (oncall) at 16:00 UTC.
sara (oncall): prepping handoff notes: actions taken, commands run, links to cached jwks and logs, CS list. Adding runbook checklist to incident.
mike (platform): added temporary dashboard panels: jwks fetch error rate, jwks payload size, auth0 edge 5xx rate by region.
cs-lead: external comms sent to affected customers. One enterprise customer wants a timeline + root cause as soon as known.
alyssa (eng-sre): Auth0 responded: they are investigating an edge cache corruption causing partial payloads for JWKS fetches in us-west-2. They recommended customers implement fallback caching — which we've done — and will push an edge fix.
sara (oncall): plan: keep fallback enabled until Auth0 confirms fix + we see 30m of clean jwks fetches. If Auth0 fixes, we'll rotate to normal behavior and perform a controlled rollout to remove fallback.
mike (platform): prepare a post-incident task: automate fallback toggle and surface it in the Console tools. Also add a mitigations doc for third-party jwks failures.
incident-bot: incident severity set to Sev2. Time to acknowledge: 00:02.
sara (oncall): handing over to jordan (oncall) in 10. Jordan — see runbook: `INC-2026-0459 handoff notes` in /incidents.
alyssa (eng-sre): one more note — we observed increased token reissue attempts from clients when they got 401s; recommend adding jittered retries client-side to avoid login storms once upstream recovers.
cs-lead: logging closure items: customer outreach follow-up, timeline, root cause summary, planned compensatory credits if SLA breached.
jordan (oncall): (joining) thanks — taking over. I'll monitor jwks fetches and keep CS looped. If Auth0 doesn't have a fix in 1h we'll consider temporary allowlist for known good keys (manual) as last resort.
sara (oncall): thanks team — great quick coordination. Leaving note and closing paging.
incident-bot: incident updated: assigned to jordan (oncall). Next update scheduled at 16:00 UTC.
